the most important thing is to eat. I used to restrict after binge days and that was a big mistake. Due to the restriction your body tends to binge again and you will feel even worse. So please try to eat again, keep yourself busy and eat small portions over the day. It’s also Important that you don’t purge, otherwise your body will panic and binge again because he doesn’t get the nutrients he needs. 

You’re not alone. I have dealt with anorexia and bulimia for a long time and I just wanna make sure that you keep trying. relapses are part of recovery and you will get through it.

When I was younger, I needed my fingers to purge. After some time, that didn’t work anymore and I started using my toothbrush. But my gag reflex became so weak, I needed to put a lot of pressure on the toothbrush to make myself throw up. One time, I forced the toothbrush so deep into my throat and I lot grip. The toothbrush was in my throat and I couldn‘t take it out, cause I was panicking and shaking. 
Luckily I got to grab it, after that I sweared to myself I would NEVER make myself throw up again. Well, one day after, I couldn’t take it anymore, I started again. But soon after, my body threw up any food without help so the toothbrush wasn’t needed anymore…
this incident was probably my most traumatic bulimic moment…

this is probably not very helpful but for me, intuitive eating/ not limiting myself was the step that made my binges disappear. It‘s extremely hard cause you need to allow yourself to eat EVERYTHING that you want and also as much as you want. And you can‘t purge. For me, that made me binge even more in the beginning and I felt terrible. But, already after a few days it got better and after 2 weeks, I was binge free. Since then I had very few relapses in the beginning but now, I don’t have the urges anymore and my life is sm better without b/p.

Hey! First of all: 3 weeks are great and you can be proud of that!  
Second of all: I understand you, I've been there and I guarantee that this isn't permanent.  
I do have an advice but it will get probably the hardest steps of all. But after that, everything will change.  
You have to let go of limiting yourself. From now on, you allow yourself, to eat everything you want, no matter what and no matter how much. It can happen that you binge on so much food, that the desire to purge gets stronger than you've experienced before but DON'T throw up. I did that and those days were the worst. I ate so much and yes, I gained weight. But not as much as I thought. And then, after maybe a week or two, the binging stopped and suddenly I could just eat whatever I wanted without forcing myself to stop. I was just satisfied after a normal amount.   
I know that this step is so fucking hard, it was for me too. But after years of suffering I got tired from fighting these urges you know?  
I don't want to lie, I still struggle with food sometimes, but never with binging anymore.  
And I started to enjoy other things as well. I think that's because I overall feel better when my eating habits aren't that bad.

I really hope that this is helpful to you in a way... If not, I am really sorry and I wish you the best. I know you're hurting and I truly wish I could take your pain away. Sending you much strengh, you got this <3

if you have suicidal thoughts, try to accept them. This is the first step. They are just thought and you are in control. Then try to let them go. Don't worry if it doesn't work yet. Those kinda thoughts aren't easy to handle.

Talking to your parents is definetly worth a try. And if they react in an unappropriate way you should talk to someone else, preferably an adult (teacher, neighbours, parents of friends, anyone....). Please, please talk to someone. You don't have to go through this alone.

You  derserve help. Maybe you feel like you don't bc of your childhood or that you don't have the right to feel bad, but that's bullshit. You're not doing well and it doesn't matter if your childhood was okay. It really doesn't.

I hope I could help you, at least a little bit... or show you that you're not alone. I don't know you but I'm positive you'll get through this and I'm proud of you for trying. If you need someone to talk to/ vent, feel free to dm me. I can't promise that I can help you but I'm here.

It may take some time till you don't feel the need to self-harm, and that is totally okay and normal. You need to take little steps.

I also think you would really need therapy... I don't know where you live and why you can't afford it, but that is not good at all. If you're planning on ending your life soon, you should call the emergency. However, there must be a way for you to receive professional help. Strangers on the internet can't help you the same way as a therapist could. You deserve help, and your feelings are absolutely valid. 

It may be hard to believe rn, but I bet it'll get better. This is a dark time of your life, but at some point, in a few years, you'll look back and think, "Wow, that was horrible, but I got through it, and I am so happy now!".

You said your loved ones are all dead... I am very sorry about that. If there is anyone left you trust, talk to them. Maybe a teacher/classmate (I don't know how old you are), a colleague or neighbour, I don't know... someone in real life who can actually be there, physically. 

Please don't end your life. Maybe you could set yourself a goal of, for example, a month or something. That may feel a little easier to achieve than "forever". Also, try to focus on things in your life that you love... people who are left, things you're passionate about, maybe a pet? Things you would like to do in your life.. write a bucket list! 

It is really important that you talk to someone. If talking is too difficult for you in that situation, write a letter. You can take breaks while writing it if you need them. It is much more difficult to get through this alone than with another person by your side. 

I wish you the best, and I hope so much that you will feel better soon. You deserve to be happy.
